question: Can the original no-PSRAM ESP32 support at least four nodes, targeting eight endpoints per node, with workloads informed by Beacon examples?
verdict: Four compact runtime guests plus memory reservations for 32 endpoints fit in the physical experiment. Functional 32-endpoint/Wi-Fi capacity remains unqualified; production slot/profile limits unchanged.
beacon_notes: Inspected existing working-tree artifacts only. Legacy env ABI/imports, setup/func or main_app exports, min1 page without explicit max. Current P3 cannot execute them unchanged. Heap-base metadata includes guest data/C stack, not runtime/native/application heap cost. Artifact size is not peak RAM.

host.experiment_sanitizers: ASan and UBSan; direct comparison disabled leak checking due to sandbox. Subsequently all 15 registered suites passed with address, fail-fast undefined-behavior and leak checking outside sandbox, including new compact capacity test. WAMR fake-stack exception retained.

esp32.board: Original ESP32 v3.0, no PSRAM, 160 MHz, IDF v5.5, serial /dev/ttyUSB0
esp32.guest: Existing runtime_guest.c recompiled with __heap_base/__data_end exports; original source unchanged
esp32.modes: two compute-only mode4 and two cancellable event-wait mode0

production_correction: Initialize pinned thread-manager temporary Vector to zero in exact-match build copy. OOM could otherwise destroy an uninitialized lock. Observed physical panic in pthread_mutex_destroy via bh_vector_destroy / safe_traverse_exec_env_list / wasm_exec_env_destroy; same sweep passed after correction. Guest-thread support remains disabled.
limits: Endpoint buffers are touched memory reservations, not active channels or traffic.
No Wi-Fi, CoAP service, artifact transfer concurrency or full deployment observer costs measured in this experiment.
Four is demonstrated residency, not maximum capacity. No universal minimum arena inferred from one guest.
Compact backing requires linker-managed layout and absence of memory.size/grow; arbitrary access to unused declared memory is not promised.
Candidate port/incidence/report layout is only statically reserved; larger wire requests/reports and revision capacity still require protocol qualification.
Beacon workloads must be adapted/rebuilt and measured with full queues and real endpoint operations before claiming the requested viability target.
The board is left running the capacity experiment.
